title: T1583.004 — Acquire Infrastructure - Server
subtitle: Watch the full bulletproof-hosting story: renting the machine, abusing it, and the reputation-hit moment the SOC can act on.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker finds a bulletproof hoster on a criminal forum, pays in crypto for a dedicated server, deploys a C2 panel and malware repository, victims connect, the SOC gets a reputation-feed hit on the server IP, and the SOC blocks, shares intel, and reports abuse.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: Shops for capacity on criminal forums, pays in crypto, and runs the operation from a separate control host.

nodes.label: Hoster
nodes.tip: A bulletproof hosting provider: sells dedicated servers and ignores abuse complaints for a premium.

nodes.label: Dedicated
nodes.tip: The rented dedicated server running the C2 panel and the malware repository on a stable IP.

nodes.label: Victim org
nodes.tip: The target company. Infected hosts beacon out and one user downloads the payload.

nodes.label: SOC
nodes.tip: The security operations center joining egress telemetry with reputation feeds and ASN intel.

steps.title: Find hoster
steps.caption: The attacker asks on a criminal forum for a bulletproof hoster and gets three offers. The selling point: abuse tickets get ignored.
steps.defender: Nothing is visible inside your estate yet. The deal, the forum thread, and the hosting order all sit outside your visibility; dark-web monitoring is the only early sensor.

steps.title: Pay in crypto
steps.caption: The attacker pays in cryptocurrency for a dedicated server under an abuse-tolerant policy. The hoster asks no business questions.
steps.defender: Still nothing on your sensors. A hosting order with crypto payment leaves no corporate trace; treat forum-advertised ranges as watchlist material.

steps.title: Deploy panel
steps.caption: The hoster provisions the machine and the attacker installs a C2 panel and a malware repository on the dedicated server.
steps.defender: First outside traces appear: a new TLS certificate on a young domain, open admin ports on a hosting IP. External scanning vendors may already see it.

steps.title: Beacons arrive
steps.caption: Infected machines inside the victim organization connect to the panel on a schedule. Each short session is a beacon.
steps.defender: Egress logs show regular small sessions from workstations to one stable hosting IP. Reputation enrichment has not flagged it yet, so pattern-based rules matter.

steps.title: Launch campaign
steps.caption: The attacker uses the same server to launch a spam and download campaign against the victim organization.
steps.defender: The mail gateway sees a burst of messages whose sending IP sits in the same hosting range. Bulk volume from hosting ASNs is a campaign marker.

steps.title: Payload download
steps.caption: A user clicks through and downloads the payload that the dedicated server hosts.
steps.defender: The proxy records an executable download from a bare hosting IP. The URL and file hash are your first hard IOCs (indicators of compromise).

fields.detail: A user clicks through and downloads the payload that the dedicated server hosts.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Reputation hit
steps.caption: The SOC reputation feed flags the server IP as part of a Spamhaus- or CINS-listed range. The egress block alert fires.
steps.defender: Now the join pays off: feed name, listing age, and the process behind every session are in one alert. Block the IP and isolate the talking hosts.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Share and watch
steps.caption: The SOC shares the indicators with the community, files an abuse report, and keeps the whole IP range under watch.
steps.defender: The hoster ignores the report, as expected. The range goes on the watchlist; the shared intel helps other defenders catch the same server earlier.
